summary.oneLiner: IMPAL is one of the leading distributors of automobile spare parts and accessories for the Indian automotive aftermarket, operating a 99-branch nationwide network as part of the TSF group.
summary.business: Incorporated in 1954, the Company operates a single-segment business of sale and distribution of automobile spare parts and accessories across India through its branch network, serving the Indian automotive aftermarket. Most of its suppliers are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) and it represents 28 leading manufacturers of the Indian automobile industry. Headquartered at Chennai, it has a nationwide footprint with presence in 23 states operating through a network of 99 branches.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for genuine aftermarket products is expected to sustain in the near future, based on the increasing vehicle park
- The outlook for the auto parts distribution industry remains moderately positive and resilient, with steady long-term growth expected despite short-term challenges
- The Indian economy is expected to grow around 6.5% in the upcoming year, with the service sector remaining the primary contributor to GDP growth
- Growth expected to continue on the back of the Company's strong presence in smaller cities, towns and rural areas
- Rising fuel prices and inflationary trends may restrict volume growth for genuine parts
- Increasing commodity prices may limit volume growth

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand the dealer network closer to consumption areas while ensuring timely availability of parts and maintaining cost efficiency, which management calls vital for sustained growth
- Continue physical branch expansion — ten new branches were opened during FY2025-26
- Leverage the Company's strong presence in smaller cities, towns and rural areas as the engine of continued growth
- Strengthen systems and processes — a new ERP system was successfully implemented during the financial year
- Remain a single-segment distributor of automobile spare parts and accessories sourced largely from Original Equipment Manufacturers
- The Company's stated governance philosophy is to enhance shareholder value while protecting the interests of all stakeholders through sound business decisions and prudent financial management. Dividends are paid in accordance with a board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy published on the Company's website; for FY2025-26 an interim dividend was paid during the year and a final dividend has been recommended for shareholder approval at the Annual General Meeting. No amount was transferred to the General Reserve during the year, and the Company accepted no public deposits. The capital structure was left unchanged — no equity shares with differential voting rights, no sweat equity and no Employee Stock Option Scheme were issued during the year, and no stock options have been issued to any Director. The Company has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company, so capital is deployed within the standalone distribution business. Remuneration policy intent is to keep the level and structure of remuneration appropriate to the expertise required, with a clear link between remuneration and performance and a balance of fixed and incentive pay for working directors, KMP and senior management; Non-Executive Directors receive sitting fees and a commission within the shareholder-approved ceiling of 1% of net profits.
- The Company is committed to reducing its environmental footprint by promoting energy-efficient practices such as the use of LED lighting, energy-saving office equipment and optimum utilisation of air-conditioning systems at the head office and across all its branches, though there was no capital investment on energy investment equipment during the year.
- The Company is not required to furnish the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) for the financial year 2025-2026, so no BRSR sustainability targets are disclosed.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: IMPAL's expansion is distribution-led rather than manufacturing-led: it expanded operations by opening ten new branches during FY2025-26, taking the network to 99 branches spread across 23 states with headquarters at Chennai. Management identifies expanding the dealer network closer to consumption areas — while ensuring timely availability of parts and maintaining cost efficiency — as the key opportunity for sustained growth, supported by its strong presence in smaller cities, towns and rural areas. A new ERP system was successfully implemented during the year. On the energy side, the Company pursues energy-efficiency initiatives such as LED lighting, energy-saving office equipment and optimum utilisation of air-conditioning at the head office and across branches, but states there was no capital investment on energy investment equipment, and it has no activity relating to technology absorption. The Company has no subsidiary, joint venture or associate company, and no manufacturing plant or capacity project is disclosed in the annual-report text provided.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Nationwide distribution footprint: presence in 23 states through a network of 99 branches, headquartered at Chennai
- Represents 28 leading manufacturers of the Indian automobile industry, with most suppliers being Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM), supporting a genuine-parts proposition
- Operating history since 1954 and lineage of the TSF group (the T.S. Santhanam branch of the erstwhile TVS group), continuing a tradition of Trust, Value and Service
- Strong presence in smaller cities, towns and rural areas, which management cites as the basis for continued growth
- Strong focus on meeting customer requirements in terms of quality, delivery, price, service and trust, with an extensive product range
- A new ERP system was successfully implemented during the financial year 2025-2026

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Fuel price and inflationary pressure on volumes — Management states that rising fuel prices and inflationary trends may restrict volume growth for genuine parts.
- Commodity price inflation — In its outlook management notes that increasing commodity prices may limit volume growth.
- Global environment / industry-level threats to auto spare parts distribution — Management states the auto spare parts distribution industry faces several significant threats, especially in the current global environment, tempering an otherwise moderately positive outlook.
- Single-segment, single-geography concentration — The Company operates in a single segment business of sale and distribution of automobile spare parts and accessories across India, so earnings depend entirely on one product-market with no segment or export diversification (the Company had no foreign exchange earnings).
- Dependence on OEM principals for supply — Most of the Company's suppliers are Original Equipment Manufacturers, making continuity of principal relationships and parts allocation central to the distribution model.
- Execution risk on parts availability and network reach — Management identifies expanding the dealer network closer to consumption areas and ensuring timely availability of parts while maintaining cost efficiency as vital for sustained growth — making distribution execution the key swing factor.
- Reliance on internal controls and risk governance as the mitigation framework — The Company relies on an Internal Control System commensurate with the size, scale and complexity of its operations, a Risk Management Committee and Risk Management Policy, and a Vigil Mechanism, with audit observations and corrective measures reported to the Audit Committee on a regular basis.
